problems.title: Printed operator decomposition does not recover the stated output-shift geometry
problems.location: Definition3.1, Extracting Principal Components and Hypothesis3.2 p3; effective rank and dominant component p4
problems.claim: Right singular vectors of W-I describe representation-shift directions; squared singular-value fractions describe shift variance.
problems.assumptions: Finite equal-weight input distributions; exact affine T(x)=Wx+b; unique affine fit in the first two witnesses. No unasserted nonlinear-fit error or input isotropy. The anisotropic witness uses all four independent-sign combinations.
problems.check: First witness X={(-1,1),(1,1),(-1,3),(1,3)}, A=e1 e2^T: all shifts in span(e1), unique leading right vector e2. Second centered X=(+-1,+-10), A=diag(2,1): operator fraction .8 versus actual e1 variance fraction1/26. Third T(x)=x+e1, A=0 omits nonzero shifts.
problems.result: Exact analytic contradictions; parent NumPy checks passed, auxiliary exact-rational checks agreed. At90% threshold operator rank2 versus data-shift rank1.
problems.counterevidence: Input-sensitivity reading is legitimate but different. Released code applies SVD to sample shifts, often recovering correct output directions; no released-code right/left bug is alleged. Actual feature directions and broad multidimensional observation may survive.
problems.impact: Invalid central mathematical recipe and interpretation linking residual geometry, effective rank and learned directions.
problems.correction: Nonzero right singular vectors of D span its row space; full right basis diagonalizes D^T D. Center D for variance; retain intercept/mean for full shift span. Population centered covariance A Sigma A^T. Does not verify empirical semantics or historical pipeline.

problems.title: Signed projection statistic does not establish late-layer likelihood or certainty growth
problems.location: Section5.2 and Figure5 p7; output_prediction_with_components.py lines280-285,325-328
problems.claim: Rising prediction log-likelihood with plateaued accuracy demonstrates reduced uncertainty in later layers.
problems.assumptions: Use exact retained statistic mean((z-mean(z))*(2y-1)), balanced binary labels, same prevalence threshold. Explicit logistic link used only to provide an admissible counterexample to the statistic-to-certainty implication.
problems.check: y=(1,1,0,0), z=(3,3,-3,-3), z'=(10,.1,-10,-.1): both100% accuracy, score3->5.05; actual logistic meanLL -.04858735->-.32222103; entropy .19086497->.34619906nats. Retained artifact33x100 has positive entries and Figure5 positive0..9scale.
problems.result: Independent calculation passed. Statistic is unbounded signed centered margin, not normalized discrete log-likelihood.
problems.counterevidence: It can measure label-aligned separation. Actual model uncertainty may decrease; no measured entropy trajectory or exact historical-run version is claimed.
problems.impact: The reported evidence does not establish a central late-layer uncertainty-reduction mechanism.
problems.correction: Relabeling as signed margin is valid; calibrated held-out likelihood/entropy and historical run binding remain unperformed.

problems.title: The stated N80 partition includes the underlying test goals in raw training data
problems.location: AppendixC.1 p16,Figure7; Section6.1 p8; ssft_dataset.py lines63-72,95-100,107-112,123-125
problems.claim: The60 STRONG REJECT test samples are completely disjoint from training, supporting unseen-query generalization.
problems.assumptions: Manuscript N80 mixture includes all313 raw STRONG REJECT goals; the60 test goals are drawn from that same corpus. Distinguish goal identity from wrapped-string identity.
problems.check: 8*80+313+347=1300 harmful training rows. For H subset G, |G|313, |H|60 and all G trained, H intersect G=H. Released five-method/default1600 constructor likewise needs400 supplemental rows atN80, includesall313, and does not filter held-out goal IDs.
problems.result: Goal-level independence fails in the specified configuration; no raw-row enumeration is fabricated.
problems.counterevidence: Held-out jailbreak strings and new formulations can remain valid; not extended to all N, every DPO ordering, exact transformed-string overlap, or false relative rankings.
problems.impact: Materially changes the core unseen-goal interpretation of the exposure/generalization experiment.
problems.correction: Reserve held-out goal identifiers across raw and transformed training sources. Necessary design specification only; no repaired dataset or rerun verified.

problems.title: The reported non-dominant-only contrast includes early dominant C1 directions
problems.location: Dominant-component notation p3;Section6 p7;Section6.1 p8;AppendixD p19
problems.claim: Suppress non-dominant components while leaving dominant components untouched to establish causal effects of indirect features.
problems.assumptions: C1 is dominant at every layer by paper definition; AppendixD states all4096 directions beforelayer10 are suppressed.
problems.check: Every full4096-direction set contains C1. Therefore the described intervention changes dominant directions too and cannot isolate the stated contrast.
problems.result: Direct text/visual contradiction, with independent logical inclusion check.
problems.counterevidence: Low harmfulness correlation may motivate a semantic indirect-feature definition, but it differs from SVD dominance. No claim early C1 actually caused the effects or that secondary features lack causal influence. The separate L14C6 result survives this specific criticism.
problems.impact: The claimed causal attribution from the aggregate intervention is unsupported by the stated controlled contrast.
problems.correction: Requires C1-preserving secondary-direction intervention and matched early-C1 control; no causal rerun performed.

problems.title: Table4 final-column denominator differs from its label
problems.claim: Last column is MSE divided by mean squared unaligned activation norm.
problems.assumptions: Use six rows exactly as printed; account for displayed rounding.
problems.check: All6 values match MSE/mean squared shift norm within .1% relative rounding. Layer31 .02151/484.2=4.442379e-5 versus printed4.443e-5; actual base ratio .02151/3526=6.100397e-6.
problems.result: Denominator label mismatch verified independently from original page and all six rows.
problems.counterevidence: Correct base ratios are even smaller. Coordinate-averaging MSE convention is unavailable; no established factor4096 error or invalidated small-error conclusion.
problems.impact: Local numeric interpretation defect without demonstrated core harm.
problems.correction: Relabel shift denominator or recompute base ratios; arithmetic verified, author adoption not requested.
